newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange's All Share Index hit a new record high on Wednesday, finishing up 21.4 points at 7,214.5 points.
Its previous high was 7,212 points, set on May 6.
Dealers said the all-share index was propelled by a slight run in industrial shares after they retraced earlier losses in active late trade, cheered by a stronger start on Wall Street.
Some futures-related trade was also responsible for industrials' skip up, they said.

"There has been a bit of a push at the close for some of our industrial shares with gold shares going the other way slightly softer," James Scott, an equities trader at stockbroking firm Societe Generale Frankel Pollack told Reuters.
"I think it's mainly futures related at this stage."
The industrials index finished up 19.2 points at 8,493.9, golds were down 5.3 points at 1,270.1 and the all-share index was up 21.4 points at 7,214.5.
Dealers said golds had failed to liven up despite a better bullion price.

"Despite gold being well about $349, they've (golds) been very disappointing. This is a very quiet day for golds. Perhaps some investors are not convinced that the gold price is going to go beyond and that's why we haven't seen some fundamental buying of the stock," one dealer said.
Volumes were moderate on the day with 736 million rand worth of shares changing hands by the close, dealers said.
They said underlying market sentiment remained positive.
"I doubt that we are going to see much more activity unless something significant happens in our markets," one dealer said.
Local March Producer Price Index, due for release on Thursday, is seen offering some direction.

Dealers said that Wednesday's stock movers included Liberty Life which ended 450 cents up at 129.50 rand on the back of an announcement by the company that its new financial year had got off to a good start with new business figures for the first quarter of 1997 more than 65 percent up on the year-ago.
"The highlight of the day has been the likes of Liberty Life. It has been lagging this market and we saw today being their strong performance," a dealer said.
De Beers finished up 75 cents at 160.50 rand on news that a deal between the South African diamond giant and Russia was imminent.
